title: Vinted Item Verification Failed: What to Do When Vinted Says Your Genuine Item Is Fake
intro: When Vinted's Item Verification fails your genuine item, the sale is cancelled, the buyer is refunded in full, the item is shipped back to you, and you can no longer re-upload that listing — and if Vinted decides the item is counterfeit, your account can be suspended on top of it. You get one appeal, within six months. Here's how the service actually works, why the failures keep happening to items bought from the brands themselves, and what to do when it happens to you.
meta_description: Vinted item verification failed your genuine item? What happens next (refund, return, can't relist), how to appeal, the counterfeit-claim evidence list, and the October 2026 terms change.
author: Supervint Team
cta_text: Never miss a genuine bargain — get alerted the second it's listed

body.heading: What "item verification failed" actually means on Vinted
paragraphs: Item Verification is an optional paid service that only the buyer can add at checkout — £10 per item, free for the seller, offered only on eligible listings (roughly £85 or more, on an eligible brand list, in clothing, bags, accessories, jewellery or shoes). Vinted's help page states it's currently available only for items traded within the UK.

When a buyer adds it, you post the item to Vinted's verification hub on a prepaid Vinted label (5 business days to ship). The team checks authenticity within 1–2 business days of arrival, and end-to-end delivery can take up to 10 business days. Vinted states plainly that the process doesn't involve the brands, and the experts aren't associated with any of them.

"Failed verification" therefore doesn't mean the brand, the police or any official body has assessed your item — it means Vinted's own team couldn't confirm authenticity. That distinction shapes everything you can do about it.

body.heading: What happens the moment your item fails verification
paragraphs: Vinted's help pages are unambiguous about the outcome. If the item fails verification, Vinted ships it back to the seller, the seller can no longer re-upload that item, and the buyer receives a full refund — the verification fee, Buyer Protection and all shipping fees — within 1–2 business days of the item being sent back.
Your money isn't at risk in this branch, because the buyer paid for the service. What's at risk is the listing and the item: it comes back to you and it can't go back on Vinted.

The more dangerous sentence is the one that follows. Vinted states a zero-tolerance policy on counterfeits and says that if sellers repeatedly list non-genuine items it will block the account definitively. In the seller threads, a failed verification is very often the first domino before a suspension.

body.heading: Why genuine items fail — what the threads actually describe
paragraphs: The complaints are strikingly consistent, and they share one feature: the seller had proof and the item was authentic. A Moncler jacket bought inside a Moncler store, submitted with the receipt, Moncler's confirmation email and matching bank transactions, failed as showing "signs of it being a fake". A Supreme hoodie bought brand new from Supreme's own website failed over the "wrong typography". A pair of Air Jordan 1s won on SNKRS and still in the Nike box failed with no explanation. A Coach bag bought from a Coach outlet "could not be authenticated"; a designer bag bought from a personal shopper failed even beside an identical store-bought one.

The reasons given are often vague, and sometimes simply wrong. One seller's dress was rejected because "the linen was not consistent" — the dress wasn't linen. Another's fully hallmarked 9ct gold ring was declared fake because "it didn't have the mark", with photos of the hallmarks attached. One seller had the identical luxury bag pass when they bought it and fail when they resold it. Receipts and invoices, in short, are often not enough on their own.
It cuts the other way too: the BBC has reported a case where a buyer paid for a designer bag that passed verification and turned out to be counterfeit.

body.heading: If Vinted accuses you of selling counterfeits, not just a failed check
paragraphs: Counterfeiting accusations are a separate, more serious track. Vinted's counterfeit policy says a listing offering a counterfeit item will be permanently removed and the account suspended, with repeated offences leading to a permanent block. Sellers describe a very short clock to respond with proof: the current terms give 24 hours, doubling to 48 hours under the terms landing in October 2026.

What gets ignored is the story. Sellers describe submitting almost 30 photographs — invoices, original packaging, barcodes, authentication holograms, interior labels, tags, close-ups of stitching and logos — and receiving a copy-paste reply stating the items are counterfeit and the decision is final. Others report bans for reselling a genuine hat and cushion bought from a UK department store, for genuine football shirts submitted with receipts, and one account with hundreds of five-star reviews banned for "fraud" with no specifics.

Vinted's authenticity help article lists what it wants to see, and it's worth matching item for item: receipt or invoice, certificate of authenticity, tags and care labels, clear photos of logos, patterns and stitching, original packaging, and date or authenticity codes. For electronics, add the serial number, warranty card and the barcode on the box.

body.heading: How to appeal — once, and how to make it count
paragraphs: You get exactly one appeal, within six months of the moderation decision. The link is in the Vinted inbox message or the official email carrying the decision, so find that message and screenshot it. Because there's no second attempt, don't send a stream of angry messages — the threads that succeed use one calm, complete appeal with everything attached at once.

Structure it as facts: what you bought, when, from where, what you paid, and what the listing showed. Attach the receipt or invoice, any order confirmation email, clear photos of tags, care labels, stitching, logos and date codes, and the original packaging if you have it. Where the brand supports it, a brand-linked authentication check such as Certilogo gives you a document of authenticity produced by someone other than you, which beats a photo of a receipt.

body.heading: If the appeal is rejected: the escalation routes that exist
paragraphs: Vinted's dispute-resolution help page lists a legal-team address for legal or regulatory issues — on the UK site, legal@vinted.co.uk — and points dissatisfied users toward external dispute resolution, naming the Centre for Effective Dispute Resolution in the UK. These are Vinted's own published routes, not forum workarounds.

For EU users, the updated terms keep the door open to EU alternative dispute resolution bodies, national consumer organisations and the courts. Vinted is regulated in Lithuania, and the threads that end in a reversal typically involve a formal complaint to the Lithuanian consumer rights authority, or — where the objection is a decision made automatically with no meaningful human involvement — the Lithuanian data protection inspectorate. EU platforms must also give a clear statement of reasons for a restriction and run an internal complaint-handling system under the Digital Services Act.

For UK sellers with meaningful money at stake, small claims court is the route that keeps appearing in the seller community — read our dedicated guide first, because the paperwork is simple but the process has to be followed properly.

body.heading: What changes on 5 October (EU) and 8 October 2026 (UK, US, Australia)
paragraphs: Vinted is updating its terms across several markets — 5 October for the EU (including France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, Austria, Spain, Portugal, Italy and Ireland) and 8 October for the UK, US and Australia. According to the independent marketplace news outlet Value Added Resource, which compared the current terms with the updated version, two changes matter directly in a verification dispute.

First, the window to provide evidence of authenticity when Vinted believes an item is counterfeit doubles from 24 hours to 48 hours. Second, Vinted gains an explicit right to destroy an item it has verified as counterfeit: the item is held for six weeks after the seller is notified, and if the seller doesn't provide satisfactory proof of authenticity or formally object within that period, they waive the right to get it back and authorise Vinted to dispose of, recycle or destroy it, without further notice or compensation.

The takeaway: the clock runs from the notification, so respond inside the window and, if you intend to challenge the result, say so formally and in writing. The mandatory Buyer Protection fee is also being renamed a "Vinted fee". Read the terms for your own market rather than a summary.

body.heading: How to make a false failure less likely
paragraphs: Before listing anything designer or branded, photograph your proof of purchase — invoice, till receipt, order email — and consider putting it in the listing photos. When you post to the verification hub, include the original authenticity documents as Vinted asks, hide your personal details, and keep a copy.
If an item fails verification, don't relist it — Vinted says you can no longer re-upload it, and sellers report that trying risks an immediate account block.

And weigh the platform before you ship. On Vinted a wrong call costs you the sale, the listing and potentially the account, with no reason you can argue against. For high-value designer pieces, many sellers now list where a failed verification comes with an explanation they can actually respond to.

faq.question: Will I still get paid if my item fails Vinted item verification?
faq.answer: No. When an item fails verification the sale is cancelled, the buyer is refunded in full — the verification fee, the Buyer Protection fee and all shipping fees — within 1–2 business days of Vinted sending the item back to you, and the item is returned to you. You don't pay for the service, because the buyer pays the £10 fee.

faq.question: Can I relist an item that failed Vinted verification?
faq.answer: Vinted states that a seller can no longer re-upload an item that has failed verification. Re-listing it risks an account block, so don't relist it on the same account.

faq.question: How long does Vinted item verification take?
faq.answer: You have 5 business days to ship the item to Vinted's hub. Once it arrives, the team usually checks authenticity within 1–2 business days and ships it on within a further 1–2 business days if it passes. Vinted says delivery can take up to 10 business days in total from the moment you ship.

faq.question: What proof should I send if Vinted says my item is counterfeit?
faq.answer: Match Vinted's own list: receipt or invoice, certificate of authenticity, tags and care labels, clear photos of logos, patterns and stitching, original packaging, and date or authenticity codes. For electronics also send the serial number, warranty card and the barcode on the box. For supported brands, a brand-linked authentication check gives you a document produced by a third party.

faq.question: Can I appeal a failed verification or a counterfeit ban on Vinted?
faq.answer: Yes — but only once, and within six months of receiving the moderation decision. The appeal link is in the Vinted inbox message or the official email carrying the decision. Make the single appeal complete and factual, with all your evidence attached, rather than sending a series of messages.

faq.question: What can I do if my Vinted appeal is rejected?
faq.answer: Vinted's dispute-resolution page lists a legal-team contact for legal or regulatory issues (legal@vinted.co.uk on the UK site) and points dissatisfied users to external dispute resolution, naming the Centre for Effective Dispute Resolution in the UK. EU users can also use national consumer bodies or EU alternative dispute resolution, and Vinted is regulated in Lithuania. For meaningful sums, UK sellers use small claims court.
